City Council -Special and Regular Meetings
AGENDA
A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
May 20, 2013
07:00 P.M.
City Hall Council Chambers
24300 Narbonne Avenue
SPECIAL CITY COUNCIL MEETING - 6:00PM
1.
OPENING CEREMONIES
a.
Call Meeting to Order
b.
Flag Salute
c.
Roll Call
2.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS Persons wishing to speak on Closed Session items or subjects other than those scheduled are requested to do so at this time. When addressing the Council, please come to the podium and give your name and address for the record. In order to conduct a timely meeting, a 5 minute time limit per person has been established. Amendments to Government Code Section 54954.2 prohibit the Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda.
SCHEDULED MATTERS
3.
COMMISSION INTERVIEWS Interview of applicants for appointment to the Planning Commission (2), re-appointment to Public Safety and Traffic Commission (1) and re-appointment/appointment to Railroad Museum Foundation Board (1).
Staff Report- item #3
ADJOURN TO REGULAR MEETING
REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING -7:00PM
4.
OPENING CEREMONIES
a.
Call Meeting to Order
b.
Flag Salute
c.
Invocation - Councilmember Traina
d.
Roll Call
5.
APPROVAL OF AGENDA
6.
PRESENTATIONS
Presentation of plaques to outgoing Planning Commissioners Maureen Kaneen and Daniel Jones.
7.
CITY MANAGER'S REPORT
8.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY COUNCIL The City Council may discuss and act upon items described under Council Comments; however, items which are not will be limited to Council reports, announcements, or requests for clarification, or factual information, or to placement of matters on the agenda for a future meeting.
9.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS Persons wishing to speak on Consent Agenda items or subjects other than those scheduled are requested to do so at this time. When addressing the Council, please come to the podium and give your name and address for the record. In order to conduct a timely meeting, a 5 minute time limit per person has been established. Amendments to Government Code Section 54954.2 prohibit the Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda.
10.
CONSENT AGENDA
All items under the Consent Agenda are considered by the Council to be routine and will be enacted by one motion in the form listed below. There may be separate discussions of these items prior to the time the Council votes on the motion. Specific items may be removed from the Consent Agenda at the request of any Councilmember or staff.
a.
Motion to Waive Further Reading

Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Special City Council Meeting held on May 6, 2013 and the Regular City Council Meeting held on May 6, 2013. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

Minutes- May 6, 2013 Regular Meeting
c.
Approval of Demands
Staff Report- item 10.C
d.
Approval of an opportunity to exchange Federal Surface Transportation Program-Local Funds (STP-L) for Flexible lACMTA STP-L Local Transportation Funds. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
Staff Report- item 10.D
e.
Approval of a Professional Services Agreement with Rincon Consultants, Inc. to prepare the initial Study/Mitigated Negative Declaration for the Islamic Center of the South Bay (ICSB) project. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
Staff Report- item 10.E
PUBLIC HEARING:
11.
DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF A DESIGN PROPOSAL FOR THE INTERSECTIONS OF 253RD STREET AT WALNUT STREET AND EBONY LANE (LOMITA TRIANGLE)
Presented by Community Services Director McPherron
Staff Report- item 11
12.
ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 2013-03 -RESTRICTIONS FOR THE USE OF LIGHT-EMITTING DIODES IN SIGNAGE Discussion and consideration of an Ordinance amending the Sections 11-1.67.04(3)(C)(III) and 11-1.67.05(B) of the Lomita Municipal Code to add restrictions for the use of Light-Emitting Diodes (LEDS) in Signage and other matters properly related thereto.
Presented by Assistant City Manager Sugano.
SCHEDULED ITEMS:
Staff Report- item 12
SCHEDULED MATTERS
13.
COMMISSION/BOARD APPOINTMENTS Report recommending that appointments be made for two (2) vacancies on the Planning Commission, one (1) term expiration on the Public Safety and Traffic Commission, and one (1) term expiration on Railroad Museum Foundation Board.
Presented by City Manager Rock.
Staff Report- item 13
14.
ASSESSMENT OF EMERGENCY POWER REQUIREMENTS Approval of a Professional Services Agreement with Design West Engineering, Inc. for Design of the Emergency Power Generator for the City Hall Building and Parks and recreation facilities in the amount not to exceed $38,328
Presented by Public Works Director Damasse
Staff Report- item 14
15.
PURCHASING CARDS PROGRAM Discussion and consideration of establishing a purchasing cards program.
Presented by Administrative Services Director Chavez.
Staff Report- item 15
ADJOURNMENT
Written materials distributed to the City Council within 72 hours of the City Council meeting are available for public inspection immediately upon distribution in the City Clerk's office at 24300 Narbonne Avenue.
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, you should contact the office of the City Clerk at 310 325-7110 (voice) or the California Relay Service. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the city to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility to this meeting.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING AND REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY
COUNCIL
May 20, 2013

6:00 P.M.- SPECIAL MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A special meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 6:00 p.m., on Monday, May
20, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Mayor Estrada led the salute to the flag.

c.  Roll Call

Those responding to the roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were City Manager Rock,
City Attorney Hagin, Assistant City Manager Sugano, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

None

  SCHEDULED MATTERS:

3.  COMMISSION INTERVIEWS

The following applicants were interviewed:
  1. Kevin Jankowski
  2. Steven Cammarata
  3. Steve Woods
  4. Bryan Wayne Matthews

ADJOURN TO REGULAR MEETING AT 6:47 P.M.

7:00 P.M.- REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL

4.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m., on Monday, May
 20, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Councilmember Savidan led the salute to the flag.

c.  Invocation

Councilmember Traina gave the invocation.

d.  Roll Call

Those responding to the roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hagin, Public Works Director Damasse,
Community Services Director McPherron, Administrative Services Director Chavez, and
Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

5.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Savidan seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

6. SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

Mayor Estrada and Councilmembers presented plaques to outgoing Planning Commissioners
Maureen Kaneen and Daniel Jones.

7. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

City Manager Rock reported that the Cypress Water Production Facility is operating well with the
current blend ratio of 70/30 (Metropolitan Water I Well Water), and that only one complaint had
been received within the past week regarding water quality. City Manager Rock added that next
week water blending will be increased to 65/35.

8. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina requested two future agenda items: consideration of establishing a policy
for texting and the use of electronic devices during City Council meetings; and discussion on
whether stating one's name and address for the record during public meetings is a necessary
requirement. These future agenda item requests failed for the lack of votes needed to place
them on the agenda.

Councilmember Traina asked staff to provide information regarding the professional
certifications of staff at the Cypress Water Production Facility (CWPF).  Furthermore,
Councilmember Traina asked staff whether carbon filtration was evaluated as a possible option
of lowering TDS levels at CWPF, to which Public Works Director Damasse responded that staff
did evaluate the option, but due to some issues associated with carbon filtration, the option was
decided not to be viable for CWPF. Councilmember Traina stated that the TDS levels of
 Metropolitan Water are 480, and EPA recommends that TDS levels be under 500;
Councilmember Traina asked if staff was evaluating other options to reduce TDS levels to under
500. Lastly, Councilmember Traina requested that this item be placed on a future agenda for
further discussion; the request failed for the lack of votes needed to be place the item on a
future agenda.

Councilmember Sanchez reported that he attended the California Contract Cities Conference
last week where he met many people and had some good conversations regarding water
issues.

Councilmember Savidan reported that he attended a meeting with representatives of the
Federal Aviation Administration during which the possibility of two other training helicopter flight
routes were discussed. Councilmember Savidan also reported that he attended the Golden
Apple Award Ceremony, which was well attended.

Councilmember Gazeley reported that he also attended the California Contract Cities
Conference, and that one of the sessions he attended was regarding earthquake preparedness.
Councilmember Gazeley urged residents to attend the Community Emergency Response Team
(CERT) trainings, and to be prepared for a disaster.

Mayor Estrada reported that she and Councilmember Savidan attended the Switzer Leaning
Center's 15th Annual South Bay's Women of the Year Awards Ceremony, where Patricia
Kromka, Lomita resident, was honored as one of the outstanding women. Mayor Estrada also
invited those in attendance to attend the Annual Sister City Fundraiser, which will be held at
Lomita Park on June 10, 2013.

9. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, stated that the City of Los Angeles had been sued by the ACLU
for ASAP cars, which are also being used in Lomita. According to Mr. McGrath, the lawsuit
stems from the fact that LAPD retains vehicle data for five years, while the Sheriff's Department
stated that they retain vehicle data indefinitely. Mr. McGrath asked City Council to be proactive
in order to keep those vehicles operating in Lomita.

George Kivett, Executive Director of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, invited those in
attendance to the Chamber's next Business Networking Mixer, which will take place at the South
Bay Health and Wellness Center on May 23, 2013, from 5:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. Mr. Kivett,
speaking in the capacity of a Lomita resident, thanked Maureen Kaneen and Daniel Jones for
their years of service as Planning Commissioners. Mr. Kivett also suggested that there be a
process for public comments prior to motions being made so that the public has an opportunity
to speak on the item before a motion is made.

10. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Traina moved to approve the Consent Agenda, but asked to pull Item 1O.D. for
discussion. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion, and stated for the record that he
would abstain from voting on Item 1O.E. The motion carried unanimously.

Item 1O.D. - In response to Councilmember Traina's question whether the funds being
requested under this item were going to be used for street repairs in accordance with the Capital
 Improvement Program, Public Works Director Damasse responded that funds would be used for
the Eshelman Project, which is one of the Capital Improvement Projects the City Council
approved earlier this year.  Councilmember Traina moved to approve Item 1O.D.
Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

Item 1O.E. - Councilmember Gazeley requested additional discussion on this item, and
Councilmember Sanchez was recused and left the Council Chambers prior to the discussion of
the item. Councilmember Gazeley stated that he had reviewed all the proposals pertaining to
this item, and one of the other proposals looked more substantial; Councilmember Gazeley
asked why staff selected the proposal from Rincon Consultants over the other proposals.
Assistant City Manager Sugano responded that staff interviewed all three firms that submitted
proposals, and Rincon Consultants had substantially more experience in this project area. The
City Council agreed to uphold the previous motion carrying the item.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Special City Council Meeting held on May
  6, 2013 and the Regular City Council Meeting held on May 6, 2013. RECOMMEND
  APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands

  d. Approval of an opportunity to exchange Federal Surface Transportation Program - Local
  Funds (STP-L) for Flexible IACMTA STP-L Local Transportation Funds. RECOMMEND
  APPROVAL.

  e. Approval of a Professional Services Agreement with Rincon Consultants, Inc. to prepare
  the initial Study/Mitigated Negative Declaration for the Islamic Center of the South Bay
  (ICSB) project. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  PUBLIC HEARINGS:

11. DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF A DESIGN PROPOSAL FOR THE
  INTERSECTIONS OF 253RD STREET AT WALNUT STREET AND EBONY LANE
  (LOMITA TRIANGLE)

Community Services Director McPherron stated that on April 1, 2013, City Council directed staff
to schedule and hold a public hearing regarding the proposed designs for the Lomita Triangle -
the intersections of 253'd Street at Walnut Street and Ebony Lane. Director McPherron went on
to provide an overview of the proposed designs for the Lomita Triangle Project, and
recommended Alternative D to the Council, with a total project budget of $120,000; Director
McPherron also recommended that Council place the Lomita Triangle Project on the City's
Capital Improvement Program so that it will be considered during the FY 2013-14 budget review.

Councilmember Traina stated the current design of the Lomita Triangle helps in controlling cut-
through traffic, and he suggested having a stop sign southbound at 253'd Street and Walnut
Street, and moving the crosswalk up to 253'd Street (at the 1900 block); Councilmember Traina
stated that this would add just the one stop sign, and everything else would be left as it is.
 Councilmember Traina also suggested moving the wheel stop at the proposed crosswalk, which
would make it ADA compliant.

During discussions, some Councilmembers were concerned that by making it a through-street,
as proposed in Alternative D, traffic would increase for 253'd Street. Irena Guilmetter, Traffic
Engineer, confirmed that the traffic count would most definitely increase, however, Ms. Guilmette
stated that traffic counts under 2,000 are acceptable for these types of streets.

Mayor Estrada opened the public hearing at 8:00 p.m.

Planning Commissioner Jones recommended that City Council approve the Lomita Triangle
design proposal proposed by staff, as a lot of people violate the right only turn.

Jeff Waters, Lomita resident, expressed his support for Alternative D, as it is a solution to the
current problem.

Ron Caropino, Lomita resident, stated that opening up the intersection is going to create more
of a hazard, and would also increase the traffic on 253'd Street. Mr.Caropino suggested
installing speed bumps on 253'd Street.

Dan Campadonia, Lomita resident, stated that Alternative D, if implemented, would have an
adverse effect, as it would funnel most of the westbound traffic through 253'd Street.

Steve Schwab, Lomita resident, stated that he was concerned with the possible increase in
traffic if intersection were to be opened up.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, believed that Alternative D would be unsafe, and stated that
Councilmember Traina's suggestion would be less costly and more efficient.

Mr. Vachi, Lomita resident, stated that he also thought that Councilmember Traina's suggestion
was the best, and asked if the proposed project money could be used to pave the streets
instead.

An anonymous speaker stated that they would be concerned with the through-traffic at 253'd
Street, as well as possible traffic congestion at the stop signs, if Alternative Dis approved.

Diana Dankin, Lomita resident, asked that stop sign be installed at 253'd Street, and added that
Councilmember Traina's proposal seemed to be the best solution.

Mayor Estrada closed the public hearing at 8:23 p.m.

Councilmember Traina made a motion to approve the design proposal he recommended earlier.
Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion. All Councilmembers agreed that it was a good,
efficient option for the Lomita Triangle. The motion carried unanimously. Mayor Estrada
suggested that staff ask the Sheriff's Department to increase their monitoring of how people
drive through the intersection.

12. ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 2013-03- RESTRICTIONS FOR THE USE OF LIGHT-
  EMITTING DIODES IN SIGNAGE
 Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that it is common for the gas stations to use digital LED
lights for gas price signage, as it makes it easier to quickly change fluctuating gas prices. But
according to Assistant City Manager Sugano, there are no regulations under current zoning
regulations for the use of LEOs in signage. Therefore, Assistant City Manager Sugano
recommended the adoption of an amendment regulating and restricting the use of LED lights, as
well as other amendments making the use of gas station terminology uniform throughout the
Municipal Code, by utilizing the single term "gasoline service station."

Councilmember Traina suggested using the term "fueling stations," instead of "gasoline service
station." All Councilmembers agreed with Councilmember Traina's suggestion.

Mayor Estrada opened the public hearing.

George Kivett, Executive Director for the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, started that this was a
well thought out amendment, and wanted to make sure that the flashing lights were not allowed.

Mayor Estrada closed the public hearing.

Councilmember Traina introduced this ordinance on the first reading, with the change in
terminology to "fueling stations." City Attorney Hagin restated that the motion was to introduce
on the first reading an amendment to Sections 11-1.67.04(3)(c)(iii) and 11-1.67.05(b), to add
restrictions for the use of light-emitting diodes (LEOs) in signage; as well as amendments to
Sections 11-1.47.02, 11-1.66.03, 11-1.49.05(6), and 11-1.58.05(4), eliminating the term "service
station," and replacing it with "fueling station;" amendments to Sections 11-1.51.02(A), 11-
1.51.06(F)(4)(c), 11-1.45.06(8)(1 )(b), and 11-1.42.05, eliminating the term "automobile service
station," and replacing it with "fueling station;" an amendment to Section 11-1.67.04(3)(c)(iv)
eliminating the term "automotive service station," and replacing it with "fueling station;"
amendments to Sections 11-1.48.04(A)(3) and 11-1.48.04(A)(4), eliminating the term
"automotive gas station," and replacing it with "fueling station;" an amendment to Section 11-
1.45.05(3) eliminating the term "automobile service station;" and an amendment to Section 11-
1.48.05(6) eliminating the term "service station." Council member Savidan seconded the motion,
which carried unanimously.

  SCHEDULED ITEMS:

13. COMMISSION/BOARD APPOINTMENTS

Councilmembers Savidan, Sanchez, and Traina nominated David Popelka to fill a vacancy on
the Planning Commission.

David Popelka was appointed to the Planning Commission.

Mayor Estrada nominated Steve Woods to fill a vacancy on the Planning Commission.
Councilmembers Gazeley, Traina, and Sanchez nominated Steven Cammarata to fill a vacancy
on the Planning Commission.

Steven Cammarata was appointed to the Planning Commission.

Councilmembers Traina, Sanchez, and Savidan nominated John Ballard to be reappointed to
the Railroad Museum Foundation Board.
 John Ballard was reappointed to the Railroad Museum Foundation Board.

Councilmembers Sanchez and Gazeley nominated Kevin Jankowski to fill the vacancy on the
Public Safety and Traffic Commission. Councilmembers Savidan and Traina nominated Gia
Stokes to fill the vacancy on the Public Safety and Traffic Commission . Mayor Estrada
nominated Kevin Jankowski to fill the vacancy on the Public Safety and Traffic Commission.

Kevin Jankowski was appointed to the Public Safety and Traffic Commission.

14. ASSESSMENT OF EMERGENCY POWER REQUIREMENTS

Mayor Estrada called for a meeting break at 8 :40 p.m. The City Council returned from the
meeting break at 8:42 p.m.

Public Works Director Damasse stated that staff solicited proposals for the design of the
emergency power generator for both the City Hall Building and Parks and Recreation Facilities,
and that two proposals had been received . According to Director Damasse, at this point staff is
only asking for the authorization to allow for the design of the emergency power generator,
totaling $35,328, of which 25% would come from the Water Fund, while the remaining 75%
would come from the General Fund. Councilmember Traina moved to approve staff's
recommendation. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

15. PURCHASING CARDS PROGRAM

Administrative Services Director Chavez provided an overview of the purchasing card program
and stated that if City Council authorizes the issuance of purchasing cards for City employees,
staff will return to Council for authorization to enter into a formal contract with the financial
institution that will be administering the program.

Discussion followed regarding the steps staff is taking in order to ensure that there will be no
abuse of the program, and that it is monitored.

Councilmember Savidan moved to recommend approval of the purchasing card program.
Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion, which carried unanimously. Councilmember
Traina asked that staff provide a report next year regarding the status of the program.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 8:53p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

  ~:;?
 Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
